why_a_log: Rates move every day, so a single number is never honest. Each entry records what was published, on what date, for which dates, under which conditions, and with which source excerpt. Rows never overwrite each other. The first two entries in this log are full dated quotes: the Venetian's own booking engine publishes an itemised breakdown (each night's rate, each night's resort fee, the tax line, the checkout total) for a specific arrival/departure pair, and both were captured on 2026-11-17.
live_lookup_limit: Which engines can be read without a browser: The Venetian's own booking engine (venetianlasvegas.com/booking?...&view=calendar) renders a complete itemised breakdown in its HTML, so dated quotes for The Venetian / The Palazzo are capturable and are logged below as of 2026-11-17. Wynn (wynnlasvegas.com/book) and the MGM property sites return an empty shell or a 404 for every dated URL tried on 2026-11-17 - their prices are built by XHR after load - so no quote is claimed for them. Quotes also fail to render for some date ranges even at the Venetian (a Dec 9-12 and a Dec 9-16 request both returned the calendar with no rate block), so a failed render is recorded as no quote, never as a price.

entries.cross_check: The two quotes caught on the same day from the same engine are internally consistent with a 13.3804% tax: 407.69 / 3,047.00 = 13.3804% and 532.51 / 3,979.75 = 13.3804%. That is an independent, live confirmation of the published Clark County 13.38% combined rate, and it proves the resort fee is itself taxed - which is the assumption the trip-cost calculator uses.
entries.caveat: A King and a Two Queen are not the same room type, so do not read the 4-night and 7-night averages as a price change for one room. Compare like-for-like: same suite type, same dates.

entries.excerpt: These rates will start as low as $119 and $209 and can be higher. Future rates are only provided out to a maximum of 150 days from the current date.
